task: Fix the known gap: tasks with no set time are placed at the end of the day. They should fill the earliest free gap (from the owner's day start) that fits them.

plan.summary: Change Scheduler._place_on_clock so untimed tasks fill the earliest free gap at or after owner.day_start instead of going after the last timed task. Timed tasks are placed first using the current logic: sort_by_time, cursor starting at day_start, and pushing later on overlap. This keeps existing timed-task placement exactly as it is. Untimed tasks are then placed one at a time, in the priority order they were chosen, into the earliest gap among the occupied intervals that fits their duration. If no gap fits, a task goes after the last occupied interval, as before. The final plan is stably sorted by integer start minutes. Only scheduling logic in pawpal_system.py changes. Tests go in tests/test_pawpal.py, and README text describing the old behavior is updated.
steps: Read pawpal_system.py, app.py, diagrams/uml.mmd, README.md and evidence/pawpal_main.txt to confirm current placement behavior, any UI text saying untimed tasks go last, and whether the UML lists private methods.

Write the new tests in tests/test_pawpal.py first, using a small helper. The helper builds an Owner with day_start='08:00' and a generous budget (e.g. 240 min) and one pet with given tasks. Run tests/test_pawpal.py and confirm the new gap tests fail on the current code.
In Scheduler._place_on_clock, split `tasks` into timed and untimed while preserving their incoming order, which is the priority order from _select_within_budget.

Place timed tasks with the existing logic unchanged: iterate sort_by_time(timed), set cursor = max(cursor, task.start_minutes), and append a ScheduledTask. Record each placed (start, end) interval in integer minutes.

Add a private helper `_earliest_free_start(self, occupied: list[tuple[int, int]], duration: int) -> int` with a docstring. It sets candidate = day_start minutes, then walks occupied intervals sorted by start. If candidate + duration <= start, it stops. Otherwise it sets candidate = max(candidate, end). It returns candidate. Back-to-back placement is allowed, so the boundary uses <=.

For each untimed task in its incoming order, call the helper and append ScheduledTask(task, _to_hhmm(start), _to_hhmm(start + duration)). Add the new interval to occupied so later untimed tasks see it.

Return the plan stably sorted by integer start minutes via _to_minutes-equivalent ints, not 'HH:MM' strings. Keep the int start alongside each item or convert while sorting so same-start timed items keep their order. Update the _place_on_clock docstring to describe the gap-filling behavior.
Run the full suite (tests/) and make sure all 20 original PawPal tests plus the agent and evaluator tests still pass.

Update README.md. Remove or mark as fixed 'Tasks with no set time are placed at the end of the day' in the known-bugs list. Update the paragraph under the main.py demo, which says Fetch in yard is pushed to the end of the day, to say this was the pre-fix output; Fetch should now land at 08:30-08:45. Update the PawPal+ and total test counts in the Setup/Testing sections. Leave evidence/*.txt untouched (they are recorded outputs) and note in the report that a human should re-run `python main.py` and pytest to refresh them.

If diagrams/uml.mmd lists private Scheduler methods, add `_earliest_free_start(occupied, duration) int`; otherwise leave it unchanged since no public API changes. If app.py has copy claiming untimed tasks go last, update that text only.

app.py (only if it has text stating untimed tasks go at the end)

test_multiple_untimed_tasks_fill_gaps_in_priority_order: timed task at 09:00 plus untimed high (30 min) and low (20 min) tasks; high gets 08:00-08:30 and low gets 08:30-08:50.
test_untimed_task_goes_after_timed_tasks_when_no_gap_fits: timed 08:00-09:00 and an untimed 15-min task; the task lands at 09:00-09:15 (fallback still works).
test_plan_with_untimed_tasks_has_no_overlaps: a mixed plan of timed and untimed tasks has no two scheduled items whose minute ranges overlap, and items are sorted by start.
risks: test_generate_daily_plan_records_conflicts depends on the order of same-time timed tasks (Luna 08:00-08:05 before Mochi 08:05-08:15). The timed path must keep its exact iteration, and the final sort must be stable and keyed on int start.
Sorting the final plan by 'HH:MM' strings would misorder end times past midnight such as '24:30'; sort by integer minutes instead.
Timed tasks with a preferred time before day_start are already pushed to day_start. The gap search must also start at day_start so untimed tasks never start earlier.
Untimed tasks could still overflow past midnight in the fallback case. That is a separate known bug and is intentionally not addressed here.

The main.py output changes (Fetch in yard moves to 08:30), so evidence/pawpal_main.txt and the README demo block become stale. The README prose is updated, but the recorded evidence files need a human re-run.
The README test counts (37 / 20) become outdated, and evidence/pytest.txt will no longer match until regenerated.
app.py may display or describe plan order; if it re-sorts the plan by string time or states that untimed tasks go last, it needs a small consistent update.
